You further state in your letter that pending receipt of funds from Ottawa, Mr. Gooderham drew upon his Agency

other than that for which they are held is a practice that should not be allowed in any case, but such Trust Funds
should be guarded jealously for the special purpose for which they were placed in trust.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Buildings, Samson's Reserve - Unsatisfactory Certificates for Progress Payments

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, March 3, 1923.

SIR, - I have to request that you kindly furnish me with an explanation of the following three payments made during
last summer to W.J. Baldry, Wetaskiwin, for material supplied and labour performed under contract in the erection of
a farming instructor's house on Samson's reserve, Hobbema agency.

On August 25th, a certificate was issued by Mr. C.W. Kirby, Indian Agent, who appears to have acted as building
inspector, to the effect that material had been supplied and labour performed to the value of $1,168.30 and
recommending an advance of $1,000 to Mr. Baldry. This advance was made by cheque No. 3035.



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 602-605) ===
<!-- page 602 -->
On September 18th a second certificate was issued by Mr. Kirby, certifying to further work having been performed on
this contract to the amount of $550 or $1,718.30 in all, and on this certificate a second advance of $1,000 was made to
Mr. Baldry by cheque No. 3278.

On October 24th a third certificate was issued certifying to further work having been performed to the value of $1,005
or $2,723.30 in all, and on this certificate a further advance of $1,150 was made to Mr. Baldry by cheque No. 4156,
making the total payments to him on account of his contract $3,150, being the full amount of his contract for $3,500,
less 10 per cent drawback.

All the above payments were certified to by Mr. Orr, your architect.

The point on which I should like an explanation is the reason for making payments to Mr. Baldry on both the second
and third certificates, considerably in excess of the amount of work performed as certified to by Mr. Kirby.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, March 5, 1923.

DEAR SIR, - I have been instructed to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 3rd inst., with reference to the
payments made last summer to Mr. W.J. Baldry, of Wetaskiwin, Alta., for the erection of a farming instructor's
residence on Samson's Indian Reserve, Hobbema Agency.

With reference to the 2nd and 3rd certificates, I beg to point out that the Department, when recommending the
payment of these accounts, was satisfied that the labour and material had been supplied, entitling the contractor to
payments as shown on the certificates.

Indian Agent Kirby, who issued the certificates, was acting as Inspector of Construction and, in issuing certificates No.
2 and 3 for the amounts as shown, must have been satisfied that the labour had been performed and the materials
supplied, warranting these payments. Also, if you refer to Certificate No. 2, you will notice that Indian Agent Kirby
states that $985 was required to complete the contract, and, as the previous payment on the contract was only $1,000, it
is quite evident that the contractor was entitled to the amount as shown on the second certificate. Furthermore, at the
time the third certificate was issued, the building was completed, as the certificate shows that no labour and material
was required to complete the contract.

Yours very truly,
J.D. MCLEAN, Asst. Deputy and Secretary.

WM. KEARNS, Asst. Auditor General, Ottawa.

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, March 23, 1923.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 5th inst. (No. 21 - 112) in reply to mine of the 3rd inst.,
with reference to the payments made during the summer of 1922 to Mr. W.J. Baldry, of Wetaskiwin, for the erection
of a farming instructor's residence on Samson's reserve, Hobbema agency.

<!-- page 603 -->
It would appear from your reply that the progress payments made by your department were based on the amount of
work shown on the building inspector's certificates as yet to be done, and not on the amount of work and material
supplied to date as shown in that certificate. I am of opinion that this was not the proper way of dealing with the
matter. The progress payments should be based solely on the value of work actually performed and material supplied
as shown by the certificate of the inspector of construction. Any discrepancy appearing between that amount, together
with the amount required to complete the contract, and the original amount of the contract should have been called to
the attention of the inspector, and an explanation or an amended certificate obtained from him. With reference to the
third certificate issued in this case, it should have been definitely stated thereon that the work was completed and that
such was a final certificate.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Payments to Inspectors of Construction for Services

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, October 29, 1923.

SIR, - On August 10th last, a certificate was issued by the Civil Service Commission for the employment, for a period
of three months from July 17th, of Mr. Wm. Swan of Punnichy as Inspector of Construction at the rate of $6.00 a day.
From an examination of the accounts I find that the following payments were made to Mr. Swan: -

Cheque 1734 - Salary for month of August and three days in July - 19 days at $6 a day $114 00
Cheque 2426 - Salary for month of September - 19 days at $7 a day                     133 00
Cheque 2943 - Salary for month of October - 10 days at $7 a day                       70 00
Cheque 3341 - Salary for month of November - 7 days at $7 a day                       49 00

Kindly inform me why after the first payment Mr. Swan was paid at the rate of $7 a day, notwithstanding the fact that
the rate authorized by the commission was only $6 a day.

I notice that the vouchers for the above payments are certified to by your architect, Mr. Orr. As Mr. Orr cannot have
personal knowledge of the number of days in each month on which Mr. Swan was present on the work I think that in
addition to his certificate I should have a statement from the Agent at Punnichy, showing the actual days in each
month for which Mr. Swan should be paid.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

<!-- page 604 -->
AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, November 8, 1929.

SIR, - On October 5th, 1922, a certificate was issued by the Civil Service Commission for the temporary employment,
for a period not exceeding six months, of Mr. Robert Paterson of Calgary as Inspector of Construction at the Blackfoot
Reserve, Gleichen, at a salary of $7.00 a day, effective from August 19th, 1923; on April 27th last a second certificate
was issued extending the period of Mr. Paterson's employment for a further period of three months from February
19th.

The classification schedule fixes the remuneration of the class "Inspector of Construction" as follows: -

Prevailing rates not exceeding $7 a day for service as required.

Monthly - 100 105 110 115 120 125 130 135 140
Yearly - 1200 1260 1320 1380 1440 1500 1560 1620 1680

I presume that it is intended from the above that when the services rendered are continuous the monthly rates shall
apply, but that when the services are not continuous the inspector may be paid up to $7 a day for services as required,
that is for services actually rendered.

From an examination of your expenditure for the fiscal year 1922 - 23 I find that Mr. Paterson was paid $7 a day for
every day from August 19th to February 28th, or $1,358 for 194 days.

From an examination of Mr. Paterson's expense accounts, he appears to have continued to reside in Calgary, making
only occasional trips to the Blackfoot Reserve. During the period ending February 28th, 1923, I find that he made 36
trips to the Reserve, viz: - 6 in September, 9 in October, 9 in November, 5 in December, 6 in January and 1 in
February. Each of these trips occupied about one and a half days, as he would require to leave Calgary early in the
afternoon and return to Calgary the following evening. I consider that Mr. Paterson was entitled to be paid only for the
days on which he was actually engaged, at the most for two days for each trip to the reserve, or for 72 days in all for
the 36 trips, instead of for 194 days as he was paid.

In addition to his salary as above Mr. Paterson was paid his expenses for each trip, amounting in all to $439.85 as
follows: -

Railway fares     $117 05
Board and lodging 118 00
Automobile hire 193 00
Postage, etc.     11 80
...               $439 85

I presume that Mr. Paterson was paid in the same way after February 28th, but as any payments to him after that date
would be paid from the current year's appropriation, they have not as yet been examined by me.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

<!-- page 605 -->
AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, December 21, 1923.

SIR, - I shall be glad to have the opinion of the Civil Service Commission on the application of the rates of
compensation given in the classification schedule for the position of Inspector of Construction.

The rates in question are as follows: -

Yearly - $1200         1260       1320 etc. to 1680.
Monthly - 100          105        110 etc. 140.
Daily -   Prevailing rates not exceeding $7 for service as required.

A number of certificates have been issued from time to time by the Commission for the appointment of Inspectors of
Construction at a daily rate. In my opinion a man appointed to this class at a daily rate is entitled to pay only for those
days on which he is actually engaged on inspection work. I find, however, that in some cases the department concerned
has paid the appointee continuously at the daily rate, whether he was or was not actually employed on each day. This
application of the daily rate brings the monthly compensation up to $210 or $217, which far exceeds the maximum of
$140 a month for continuous employment.

I should like to be informed as to whether my view of the matter, as expressed above, is or is not, in the opinion of the
Commission, the correct one.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Secretary, Civil Service Commission, Ottawa.

CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION, OTTAWA, December 27, 1923.

Re: Compensation for the Class "Inspector of Construction"

DEAR SIR, - With reference to your letter of the 21st instant inquiring as to the opinion of the Commissioners
regarding the daily rate of pay for the above class, I am directed to inform you that your understanding of the matter
coincides with that of the Commissioners, i.e., that a man appointed to a position in this class at a daily rate is entitled
to pay only for those days on which he is actually engaged on inspection work.

Yours truly,
W. FORAN, Secretary.

Assistant A.G.

Disposal of Stock and Equipment, Dunbow (St. Joseph's) Industrial School

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, March 27, 1923.

SIR, - I understand that the Dunbow Indian Industrial School, near High River, Alberta, was recently closed, and that
the stock and equipment was disposed of by one of your inspectors. Kindly let me have a copy of any report that may
have been made by your inspector with regard to the disposal of the assets of this school, giving the amount realized
from the sale with the disposal of the resulting funds, and also what part, if any, of the stock and equipment was
disposed of otherwise than by sale.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.
